name: V13700
full_name: Dual Operational Transconductance Amplifier with Linearizing Diodes and Buffers
description: Two current-controlled transconductance amplifiers with differential inputs and push-pull outputs, plus linearizing diodes and high-impedance output buffers. Gain is set by the amplifier bias current (IABC) rather than a feedback network, which makes it the workhorse of voltage-controlled amplifiers and filters. Coolaudio's in-production equivalent of the LM13700. Unlike the LM13600, the buffer input bias currents (and so their output DC levels) are independent of IABC.

pins.name: IABC A
pins.description: amplifier bias current input, sets gain of A

pins.name: V-
pins.description: negative supply (NOTE: pin 6, not a corner pin)

pins.name: V+
pins.description: positive supply (NOTE: pin 11, not a corner pin)

pins.name: IABC B
pins.description: amplifier bias current input, sets gain of B

extra.vs_LM13600: buffer input bias currents (and output DC levels) are independent of IABC

typical_application: Voltage-controlled amplifiers (VCA) and voltage-controlled filters (VCF), plus tremolo, compressors and modulation effects. Gain follows IABC, so a control voltage into the bias pin becomes the gain control. The backbone chip of synth-DIY and analog pedal VCAs.
gotchas: V- is pin 6 and V+ is pin 11, NOT the corner pins. Wiring the rails to pins 8/16 out of habit is the classic mis-wire on this chip
gain is set by the bias current IABC (pins 1 and 16), not by a feedback network; it is a current-controlled amplifier
keep IABC at 2mA or below, and always feed it through a resistor from the control voltage, never straight from a rail
the OTA input wants millivolts, not volts: attenuate hard going in (typically to tens of mV) or it distorts. The linearizing diodes buy you headroom back
the raw amplifier output is a current; the on-chip buffers (Darlington followers) are there to drive real loads. Use them
V13700M is SOIC-16 surface mount, V13700D is DIP-16; the M will not breadboard without an adapter
notes: Pins and specs checked against Coolaudio's own V13700D/M datasheet, supplied by the user. The pin diagram in that sheet confirms V- on pin 6 and V+ on pin 11.
